message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Compute Engine VM with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
(If you’re actually on AWS, replace “gcloud” with “aws ec2 run-instances” and use the appropriate AMI.)

---

## 1️⃣  Prerequisites

| Step | What you need | How to do it |
|------|---------------|--------------|
| 1 | **Google Cloud SDK** (`gcloud`) installed | `curl https://sdk.cloud.google.com | bash` (or download from <https://cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install>) |
| 2 | **Project ID** | `PROJECT_ID=$(gcloud config get-value project)` |
| 3 | **Billing enabled** on the project | <https://console.cloud.google.com/billing> |
| 4 | **Compute Engine API** enabled | `gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com` |
| 5 | **Service account key** (if you’ll use REST) | `gcloud iam service-accounts keys create key.json --iam-account=YOUR_SA@${PROJECT_ID}.iam.gserviceaccount.com` |

> **Tip:** For quick testing, you can use the *default* service account that comes with a new project.

---

## 2️⃣  Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Variables – change these to your own values
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-demo"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports RTX A6000
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8" # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
    --zone="$ZONE" \
    --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=50GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-balanced \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --accelerator=count=1,type=nvidia-a6000 \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: add a startup script
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts` | Uses the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud` | Image is hosted in the official Ubuntu project |
| `--boot-disk-size=50GB` | Minimum size for the boot disk (you can increase if you need more space) |
| `--accelerator=count=1,type=nvidia-a6000` | Adds one RTX A6000 GPU |
| `--maintenance-policy=MIGRATE` | Allows live migration during maintenance windows |
| `--scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform` | Grants full Cloud Platform access (adjust scopes if you want tighter security) |

> **Note:** The RTX A6000 is only available in certain zones (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`). Check availability with `gcloud compute accelerator-types list`.

---

## 3️⃣  Using the REST API (cURL)

If you prefer to hit the REST endpoint directly (useful for automation scripts or CI/CD pipelines), here’s a minimal example:

```bash
# Set variables
PROJECT_ID="your-gcp-project-id"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-demo"

# Load OAuth 2.0 token (replace with your own method)
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

# Build the JSON payload
read -r -d '' PAYLOAD <<EOF
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 50,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-balanced"
      }
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "MIGRATE"
  },
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ]
}
EOF

# Make the request
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$PAYLOAD"
```

> **Important:**  
> • Replace `your-gcp-project-id` with your actual project ID.  
> • Ensure the service account you’re using has the **Compute Admin** role (or at least `compute.instances.create`).  
> • The `access_token` expires after ~1 hour; refresh it as needed.

---

## 4️⃣  Verifying the Instance

After creation, you can check the status:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe "$INSTANCE_NAME" --zone="$ZONE" --format='table(name, status, machineType, disks[].deviceName, guestAccelerators[].acceleratorType)'
```

You should see something like:

```
NAME            STATUS  MACHINE TYPE                     DISKS           ACCELERATORS
rtx-a6000-demo  RUNNING n1-standard-8 (8 vCPU, 30 GB)  boot-disk-1    nvidia-a6000
```

---

## 5️⃣  Optional: Adding a Startup Script

Create a file called `startup.sh` (make it executable):

```bash
#!/bin/bash
apt-get update
apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535   # or the latest driver version
```

Then pass it via `--metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh` in the `gcloud` command above. This ensures the NVIDIA driver is installed automatically when the VM boots.

---

## 6️⃣  Cleaning Up

To avoid unwanted charges, delete the instance when you’re done:

```bash
gcloud compute instances delete "$INSTANCE_NAME" --zone="$ZONE" --quiet
```

---

### Quick Reference Cheat Sheet

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `gcloud compute instances create ...` | Launches the VM via CLI |
| `curl -X POST ...` | Same thing via REST |
| `gcloud compute instances describe ...` | View details |
| `gcloud compute instances delete ...` | Clean up |

Feel free to copy/paste the snippets into your terminal or script. Happy GPU computing!
